q: The environment is the surroundings comprising of hydrosphere, lithosphere, atmosphere and ____.
e: The environment is the surroundings comprising of hydrosphere, lithosphere, atmosphere and biosphere. Biosphere is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In the natural matter cycling, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and sulphur take a variety of chemical forms and may exist for a long period in the atmosphere, on land, in water or beneath the Earth's ____.
e: In the natural matter cycling, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and sulphur take a variety of chemical forms and may exist for a long period in the atmosphere, on land, in water or beneath the Earth's surface. Surface is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The pathways that allow different chemical substances to move through living and non-living forms and their locations in the biosphere are called a ____ cycle.
e: The pathways that allow different chemical substances to move through living and non-living forms and their locations in the biosphere are called a biogeochemical cycle. A biogeochemical cycle moves an element through rocks, water, air, and living things.

q: The cycling of elements is interconnected with the water ____.
e: The cycling of elements is interconnected with the water cycle. Cycle is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Most of the Earth's carbon is stored in rocks and ____.
e: Most of the Earth's carbon is stored in rocks and sediments. Sediments is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The processes involved in the carbon cycle are photosynthesis, respiration, exchange, fossilisation, sedimentation, and ____.
e: The processes involved in the carbon cycle are photosynthesis, respiration, exchange, fossilisation, sedimentation, and combustion. In photosynthesis plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to make food, and oxygen comes out as a product.

q: Plants constantly exchange carbon with the atmosphere by absorbing carbon dioxide during ____.
e: Plants constantly exchange carbon with the atmosphere by absorbing carbon dioxide during photosynthesis. In photosynthesis plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to make food, and oxygen comes out as a product.

q: Respiration is the process of gas exchange between the atmosphere and living ____.
e: Respiration is the process of gas exchange between the atmosphere and living organisms. Organisms is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In the fossilisation process, the animal and plant residues become sediment and eventually turn into rock and ____.
e: In the fossilisation process, the animal and plant residues become sediment and eventually turn into rock and minerals. Minerals is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The nitrogen cycle involves the following steps: nitrogen fixation, nitrification, nitrogen assimilation, ammonification, and ____.
e: The nitrogen cycle involves the following steps: nitrogen fixation, nitrification, nitrogen assimilation, ammonification, and denitrification. Denitrification is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Unlike many other cycling elements, phosphorus cannot be found in the ____.
e: Unlike many other cycling elements, phosphorus cannot be found in the air. Air is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Phosphorus is an essential nutrient for plants and animals in the form of ions $PO_4^{3-}$ and ____.
e: Phosphorus is an essential nutrient for plants and animals in the form of ions PO43- and HPO42-. HPO42- is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Phosphorus is also a building block of certain parts of the human including DNA and animal bodies, such as bones and ____.
e: Phosphorus is also a building block of certain parts of the human including DNA and animal bodies, such as bones and teeth. Teeth is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In the soil, phosphorus occurs as rock phosphate, calcium phosphate, iron phosphate, or aluminium ____.
e: In the soil, phosphorus occurs as rock phosphate, calcium phosphate, iron phosphate, or aluminium phosphate. Phosphate is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Phosphate salts that are released from rocks through weathering dissolve in water present in soil and will be absorbed by ____.
e: Phosphate salts that are released from rocks through weathering dissolve in water present in soil and will be absorbed by plants. Plants is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Marine birds play a unique role in the phosphorus cycle, as they take phosphorus-containing fish out of the ocean and return to land, where they ____.
e: Marine birds play a unique role in the phosphorus cycle, as they take phosphorus-containing fish out of the ocean and return to land, where they defecate. The phosphorus cycle moves phosphorus through rocks, water, and living things, with no long-lived gas phase.

q: Their ____ contains a high level of phosphorus and in this way, marine birds return phosphorus from the ocean to the land.
e: Their guano contains a high level of phosphorus and in this way, marine birds return phosphorus from the ocean to the land. Guano is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The sulphur cycle moves through the rocks, water bodies, atmosphere and ____ systems.
e: The sulphur cycle moves through the rocks, water bodies, atmosphere and living systems. The sulphur cycle moves sulphur among rocks, water, air, and organisms.

q: Sulphur is one of the components that make up proteins and ____.
e: Sulphur is one of the components that make up proteins and vitamins. Vitamins is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: When sulphur dioxide enters the atmosphere, it will react with oxygen to produce sulphur trioxide gas, or with other chemicals in the atmosphere, to produce sulphur ____.
e: When sulphur dioxide enters the atmosphere, it will react with oxygen to produce sulphur trioxide gas, or with other chemicals in the atmosphere, to produce sulphur salts. Salts is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Sulphur dioxide reacts with water to produce sulphuric acid (____).
e: Sulphur dioxide reacts with water to produce sulphuric acid (H2SO4). H2SO4 is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Sulphuric acid may also be produced from dimethyl sulphide emitted to the atmosphere by ____ species.
e: Sulphuric acid may also be produced from dimethyl sulphide emitted to the atmosphere by plankton species. Plankton is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: All these substances will settle back onto the Earth, or react with rain and fall back onto the Earth as acid ____.
e: All these substances will settle back onto the Earth, or react with rain and fall back onto the Earth as acid deposition. Deposition is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Carbon dioxide is released into the atmosphere by animal ____ practices.
e: Carbon dioxide is released into the atmosphere by animal husbandry practices. Husbandry is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Burning fossil fuels, deforestation, changing land use, and using limestone to make concrete transfer significant quantities of carbon into the atmosphere ____.
e: Burning fossil fuels, deforestation, changing land use, and using limestone to make concrete transfer significant quantities of carbon into the atmosphere rapidly. Rapidly is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The ocean absorbs much of the carbon dioxide that is released from burning fossil fuels, lowering the ocean's pH through a process called ocean ____.
e: The ocean absorbs much of the carbon dioxide that is released from burning fossil fuels, lowering the ocean's pH through a process called ocean acidification. pH is the negative log of the hydrogen-ion concentration, so a lower pH means more acidic.

q: Ocean acidification interferes with the ability of marine organisms to build their shells and ____.
e: Ocean acidification interferes with the ability of marine organisms to build their shells and skeletons. Ocean acidification is the long-term drop in seawater pH as the ocean takes up extra CO2.

q: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus that enter the ecosystem from fertiliser runoff and from sewage cause excessive growth of ____.
e: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus that enter the ecosystem from fertiliser runoff and from sewage cause excessive growth of algae. Algae is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The subsequent death and decay of these aquatic plants deplete dissolved ____, which leads to the death of aquatic organisms.
e: The subsequent death and decay of these aquatic plants deplete dissolved oxygen, which leads to the death of aquatic organisms. Oxygen is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The burning of large quantities of fossil fuels, especially coal, releases larger amounts of hydrogen ____ gas into the atmosphere.
e: The burning of large quantities of fossil fuels, especially coal, releases larger amounts of hydrogen sulphide gas into the atmosphere. Sulphide is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The extraction of metals such as copper, lead, and zinc from sulphur-containing ores releases sulphur ____.
e: The extraction of metals such as copper, lead, and zinc from sulphur-containing ores releases sulphur dioxide. Dioxide is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The clean and green environment implies the absence of pollution and a better quality of ____.
e: The clean and green environment implies the absence of pollution and a better quality of life. Life is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Green technology is an environmentally friendly technology that builds products and systems to conserve natural resources and the ____.
e: Green technology is an environmentally friendly technology that builds products and systems to conserve natural resources and the environment. Environment is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Green chemistry is the design of chemical products and processes that reduce or eliminate the use or generation of ____ substances.
e: Green chemistry is the design of chemical products and processes that reduce or eliminate the use or generation of hazardous substances. Green chemistry designs products and processes so they make less hazardous waste.

q: A green synthesis which is used in green chemistry also helps reduce harmful gas emissions, conserve water, reduce waste and utilise less consumption of ____.
e: A green synthesis which is used in green chemistry also helps reduce harmful gas emissions, conserve water, reduce waste and utilise less consumption of energy. Physical state changes still move energy even though the substance stays the same chemically.

q: The 7 R's of a green environment for sustainable development are Rethink, Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, Repair, Regift, and ____.
e: The 7 R's of a green environment for sustainable development are Rethink, Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, Repair, Regift, and Recycle. Recycle is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Heavy metals are metals with high density and toxic effects even at very low ____.
e: Heavy metals are metals with high density and toxic effects even at very low concentrations. Concentrations is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Pure arsenic is rarely found in nature and is not very toxic, but it can be oxidised easily in humid air and becomes toxic by conversion to arsenic ____.
e: Pure arsenic is rarely found in nature and is not very toxic, but it can be oxidised easily in humid air and becomes toxic by conversion to arsenic anhydride. Anhydride is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Arsenic is mostly found in the form of +3 and +5 oxidation states but is not in ____ form in nature.
e: Arsenic is mostly found in the form of +3 and +5 oxidation states but is not in elemental form in nature. Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: The desorption and dissolution of arsenic from arsenic rich rocks and minerals are the main sources of groundwater contamination and ____.
e: The desorption and dissolution of arsenic from arsenic rich rocks and minerals are the main sources of groundwater contamination and soil. Soil is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Compounds such as calcium arsenide, lead arsenide and sodium arsenate are used for the production of paint, glass, ceramics, and ____.
e: Compounds such as calcium arsenide, lead arsenide and sodium arsenate are used for the production of paint, glass, ceramics, and semiconductors. Semiconductors is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Sodium arsenate is used to kill some parasites in fruit cultivation and ____ growing.
e: Sodium arsenate is used to kill some parasites in fruit cultivation and potato growing. Potato is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Cadmium is released into the atmosphere predominantly as elemental cadmium and cadmium ____.
e: Cadmium is released into the atmosphere predominantly as elemental cadmium and cadmium oxide. Oxide is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Tobacco ____ is also a significant source of cadmium exposure.
e: Tobacco smoking is also a significant source of cadmium exposure. Smoking is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Various salts of cadmium are commonly used in electronic cells, accumulators, porcelain, nuclear materials, amalgam in dentistry, plastic, metal coating, vacuum tubes, and ____ materials.
e: Various salts of cadmium are commonly used in electronic cells, accumulators, porcelain, nuclear materials, amalgam in dentistry, plastic, metal coating, vacuum tubes, and photovoltaic materials. Photovoltaic is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Lead enters the atmosphere largely in the exhaust fumes from internal combustion ____.
e: Lead enters the atmosphere largely in the exhaust fumes from internal combustion engines. Engines is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The primary use of lead is in the manufacture of batteries, and in the production of paint, alloys and metal products in the ____.
e: The primary use of lead is in the manufacture of batteries, and in the production of paint, alloys and metal products in the industry. Industry is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: An increased level of lead in the environment can result in decreased growth and reproduction in plants and animals, and ____ effects in vertebrates.
e: An increased level of lead in the environment can result in decreased growth and reproduction in plants and animals, and neurological effects in vertebrates. Neurological is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Inorganic mercury can be transformed into methylmercury by microorganisms such as phytoplanktons and ____.
e: Inorganic mercury can be transformed into methylmercury by microorganisms such as phytoplanktons and fungi. Fungi is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Methylmercury then ____ in fish and shellfish.
e: Methylmercury then bioaccumulates in fish and shellfish. Bioaccumulates is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The source of exposure to low levels is mercury released from amalgam from the panning of gold and fillings in ____.
e: The source of exposure to low levels is mercury released from amalgam from the panning of gold and fillings in teeth. Teeth is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Mercury may have toxic effects on the nervous, digestive and immune systems, and on the lungs, kidneys, skin, eyes, and development of the child in utero and early in ____.
e: Mercury may have toxic effects on the nervous, digestive and immune systems, and on the lungs, kidneys, skin, eyes, and development of the child in utero and early in life. Life is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A pesticide is a substance that kills a pest, or it prevents or reduces the damage a pest may ____.
e: A pesticide is a substance that kills a pest, or it prevents or reduces the damage a pest may cause. Cause is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Some common pesticide families include organophosphates, organochlorines, carbamates and thiocarbamates, and ____.
e: Some common pesticide families include organophosphates, organochlorines, carbamates and thiocarbamates, and pyrethroids. Pyrethroids is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Adsorption occurs because of the attraction between a chemical and soil ____.
e: Adsorption occurs because of the attraction between a chemical and soil particles. Particles is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Positively charged pesticide molecules are attracted to and can bind to negatively charged ____ particles.
e: Positively charged pesticide molecules are attracted to and can bind to negatively charged clay particles. Clay is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The transfer includes processes that move the pesticide away from the target site, such as volatilisation, spray drift, runoff, leaching, absorption and crop ____.
e: The transfer includes processes that move the pesticide away from the target site, such as volatilisation, spray drift, runoff, leaching, absorption and crop removal. Removal is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Degradation is the process of pesticide breakdown after ____.
e: Degradation is the process of pesticide breakdown after application. Application is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Pesticides are broken down by microbes, chemical reactions, and ____.
e: Pesticides are broken down by microbes, chemical reactions, and photodegradation. Photodegradation is breakdown caused by sunlight.

q: Persistent organic pollutants (POPs) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are two of the most insidious forms of toxic ____.
e: Persistent organic pollutants (POPs) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are two of the most insidious forms of toxic contamination. Volatile organic compounds evaporate easily and can pollute air.

q: POPs are carbon-based organic compounds that have the special abilities to be long-lasting and to resist breakdown into safer ____.
e: POPs are carbon-based organic compounds that have the special abilities to be long-lasting and to resist breakdown into safer substances. Persistent organic pollutants last a long time in the environment because they resist breakdown.

q: POPs include industrial chemicals like polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) and pesticides like dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane (____).
e: POPs include industrial chemicals like polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) and pesticides like dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane (DDT). Persistent organic pollutants last a long time in the environment because they resist breakdown.

q: POPs are chemically stable, remain intact in the environment for long periods, and are ____ in nature.
e: POPs are chemically stable, remain intact in the environment for long periods, and are lipophilic in nature. Persistent organic pollutants last a long time in the environment because they resist breakdown.

q: Therefore, POPs accumulate in the fatty tissue of living organisms and reside for a longer period of time finally affecting humans and ____.
e: Therefore, POPs accumulate in the fatty tissue of living organisms and reside for a longer period of time finally affecting humans and wildlife. Persistent organic pollutants last a long time in the environment because they resist breakdown.

q: VOCs are organic chemicals that pollute the air and be absorbed or inhaled by humans, animals and ____.
e: VOCs are organic chemicals that pollute the air and be absorbed or inhaled by humans, animals and plants. Volatile organic compounds evaporate easily and can pollute air.

q: Under sunlight, VOCs react with nitrogen oxides emitted mainly from vehicles, power plants and industrial activities to form ____.
e: Under sunlight, VOCs react with nitrogen oxides emitted mainly from vehicles, power plants and industrial activities to form ozone. Volatile organic compounds evaporate easily and can pollute air.

q: The accumulation of ozone, fine particulates and other gaseous pollutants results in smog that reduces ____.
e: The accumulation of ozone, fine particulates and other gaseous pollutants results in smog that reduces visibility. Visibility is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The burning of plastics releases toxic gases like dioxins, furans, mercury and polychlorinated biphenyls into the ____.
e: The burning of plastics releases toxic gases like dioxins, furans, mercury and polychlorinated biphenyls into the atmosphere. Atmosphere is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Radioactive pollution is the result of released radionuclides in the ____.
e: Radioactive pollution is the result of released radionuclides in the environment. Environment is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A radionuclide is an atom with an unstable nucleus which has excessive ____.
e: A radionuclide is an atom with an unstable nucleus which has excessive energy. Physical state changes still move energy even though the substance stays the same chemically.

q: Radioactivity is a spontaneous process of decay or disintegration of heavy nuclei generating different types of radiation such as alpha particles, beta particles and gamma ____.
e: Radioactivity is a spontaneous process of decay or disintegration of heavy nuclei generating different types of radiation such as alpha particles, beta particles and gamma rays. Radioactivity is when an unstable nucleus throws out alpha, beta, or gamma radiation to lose energy.

q: These radiations including X-rays are called ____ radiation.
e: These radiations including X-rays are called ionising radiation. Ionising is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Alpha particles can be blocked by a few pieces of ____.
e: Alpha particles can be blocked by a few pieces of paper. Paper is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Beta particles pass through paper but are stopped by aluminium ____.
e: Beta particles pass through paper but are stopped by aluminium foil. Foil is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Low energy beta particles may penetrate the superficial layer of skin, whereas high energy beta particles will penetrate the skin a centimetre or ____.
e: Low energy beta particles may penetrate the superficial layer of skin, whereas high energy beta particles will penetrate the skin a centimetre or more. More is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Gamma rays are the most difficult to stop and require concrete, lead, or other heavy shielding to block ____.
e: Gamma rays are the most difficult to stop and require concrete, lead, or other heavy shielding to block them. Them is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Gamma rays and X-rays can cause severe damage to the ____.
e: Gamma rays and X-rays can cause severe damage to the cell. Cell is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The majority of background radiation occurs naturally from minerals and a small fraction comes from man-made ____.
e: The majority of background radiation occurs naturally from minerals and a small fraction comes from man-made elements. Background radiation is the ionising radiation that is already around you from rocks, air, and space.

q: Naturally occurring radioactive minerals in the ground, soil, and water produce background ____.
e: Naturally occurring radioactive minerals in the ground, soil, and water produce background radiation. Radiation is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Cosmic radiation from space also contributes to the background radiation around ____.
e: Cosmic radiation from space also contributes to the background radiation around us. Background radiation is the ionising radiation that is already around you from rocks, air, and space.

q: A trace amount of radionuclides, uranium and thorium, are naturally found on the ____.
e: A trace amount of radionuclides, uranium and thorium, are naturally found on the Earth. Earth is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Traces of radioactive materials can be found in the body, mainly naturally occurring potassium-____.
e: Traces of radioactive materials can be found in the body, mainly naturally occurring potassium-40. 40 is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The radioactive gas, radon, can be found at higher levels in the air in houses and other buildings, as well as in water from underground ____.
e: The radioactive gas, radon, can be found at higher levels in the air in houses and other buildings, as well as in water from underground sources. Sources is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Prolonged exposure to radon gas can cause lung ____.
e: Prolonged exposure to radon gas can cause lung cancer. Cancer is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Uranium-235, americium-241, and plutonium-239 are fissile materials produced from a breeder ____.
e: Uranium-235, americium-241, and plutonium-239 are fissile materials produced from a breeder reactor. Reactor is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Ionisation smoke detectors use americium-241 as a source of alpha ____.
e: Ionisation smoke detectors use americium-241 as a source of alpha particles. Particles is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Alpha particles from the americium source ionise air ____.
e: Alpha particles from the americium source ionise air molecules. Molecules is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: There is no health threat from ionisation smoke detectors as long as the detector is not damaged and used as ____.
e: There is no health threat from ionisation smoke detectors as long as the detector is not damaged and used as directed. Directed is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A well-known use of carbon-14 is radiocarbon dating which can be used to date wooden and organic objects, especially in ____.
e: A well-known use of carbon-14 is radiocarbon dating which can be used to date wooden and organic objects, especially in archaeology. Archaeology is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Uranium-235 is used as fuel for nuclear power plants and naval nuclear propulsion ____.
e: Uranium-235 is used as fuel for nuclear power plants and naval nuclear propulsion systems. Systems is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Caesium-137 is used as a tracer in medical radiation therapy devices for treating ____.
e: Caesium-137 is used as a tracer in medical radiation therapy devices for treating cancer. Cancer is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Caesium-137 is also used in industrial gauges that detect the flow of liquid through ____.
e: Caesium-137 is also used in industrial gauges that detect the flow of liquid through pipes. Pipes is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Radioactive reactors use fissile heavy atoms as fuel instead of fossil ____.
e: Radioactive reactors use fissile heavy atoms as fuel instead of fossil fuels. Fuels is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Nuclear bombs are weapons having massive destructive ____.
e: Nuclear bombs are weapons having massive destructive power. Power is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The explosion of a nuclear weapon releases a combination of heat, blast waves and ____.
e: The explosion of a nuclear weapon releases a combination of heat, blast waves and radiation. Radiation is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Radionuclides found in water are potassium-40, radium-226 and radium-____.
e: Radionuclides found in water are potassium-40, radium-226 and radium-228. 228 is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Water bodies are also polluted by accidental leakage of waste material from uranium and thorium mines, nuclear power plants and ____.
e: Water bodies are also polluted by accidental leakage of waste material from uranium and thorium mines, nuclear power plants and industries. Industries is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Radioactive materials can enter the human body through water and food and may be accumulated in blood and certain vital ____.
e: Radioactive materials can enter the human body through water and food and may be accumulated in blood and certain vital organs. Organs is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Accumulated radioactive materials cause tumours and ____.
e: Accumulated radioactive materials cause tumours and cancer. Cancer is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Chemistry plays an essential role to achieve the United Nations Sustainable Development ____.
e: Chemistry plays an essential role to achieve the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Goals is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The agricultural sustainability is the area that requires green chemistry strategies in the manufacturing of ____.
e: The agricultural sustainability is the area that requires green chemistry strategies in the manufacturing of agrochemicals. Green chemistry designs products and processes so they make less hazardous waste.

q: Organic farming uses fertilisers of organic origin such as compost manure, green manure, and bone meal instead of chemical ____.
e: Organic farming uses fertilisers of organic origin such as compost manure, green manure, and bone meal instead of chemical fertilisers. Fertilisers is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Instead of using chemical-based pesticides, plant-based pesticides that have minimum risks including essential oils and insecticidal soaps can be ____.
e: Instead of using chemical-based pesticides, plant-based pesticides that have minimum risks including essential oils and insecticidal soaps can be used. Used is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The neem leaves consist of insecticidal ingredients and they can be used as an ____.
e: The neem leaves consist of insecticidal ingredients and they can be used as an insecticide. Insecticide is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Agrochemists have developed formulation technology to produce plant-based ____.
e: Agrochemists have developed formulation technology to produce plant-based pesticides. Pesticides is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Generally, a plant-based pesticide forms a stable water soluble complex with nutrient molecules to prevent mineralisation in the soil and facilitate foliar application directly to the ____.
e: Generally, a plant-based pesticide forms a stable water soluble complex with nutrient molecules to prevent mineralisation in the soil and facilitate foliar application directly to the leaves. Leaves is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Plant-based insecticidal soaps can be used either on indoor plants or on outdoor plants, including vegetables to eliminate small soft-bodied ____.
e: Plant-based insecticidal soaps can be used either on indoor plants or on outdoor plants, including vegetables to eliminate small soft-bodied insects. Insects is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Insecticidal soaps leave no nasty residue, are non-toxic to animals and birds, and do not harm beneficial ____.
e: Insecticidal soaps leave no nasty residue, are non-toxic to animals and birds, and do not harm beneficial insects. Insects is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The municipal and non-hazardous industrial wastes have been converted to energy by direct ____.
e: The municipal and non-hazardous industrial wastes have been converted to energy by direct burning. Burning is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In waste gasification, much of the organic content wastes in the reactor produce a mixture of hydrogen and carbon ____.
e: In waste gasification, much of the organic content wastes in the reactor produce a mixture of hydrogen and carbon monoxide. Monoxide is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The gas mixture is sent to a catalytic system that converts it to ethanol and methanol or other liquid fuels or ____.
e: The gas mixture is sent to a catalytic system that converts it to ethanol and methanol or other liquid fuels or chemicals. Chemicals is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Solar, wind, hydroelectric, biomass, biorefineries, geothermal, and tidal energy are important resources for future sustainable ____.
e: Solar, wind, hydroelectric, biomass, biorefineries, geothermal, and tidal energy are important resources for future sustainable development. Development is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Ethanol is the most important alcohol which can be produced by converting the sugar content of any starchy material into alcohol with the evolution of carbon ____.
e: Ethanol is the most important alcohol which can be produced by converting the sugar content of any starchy material into alcohol with the evolution of carbon dioxide. Dioxide is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Productions of ethanol are from lignocellulosic materials such as corncob, cornstalk, cornhusk, sugarcane bagasse and sugarcane ____.
e: Productions of ethanol are from lignocellulosic materials such as corncob, cornstalk, cornhusk, sugarcane bagasse and sugarcane bark. Bark is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Biodiesel oil is produced from cultivated plant ____.
e: Biodiesel oil is produced from cultivated plant oil. Biodiesel is a diesel-like fuel made from plant or animal fats as long-chain fatty acid esters.

q: Biodiesel oil is synthesised from plant oils by removing the by-product glycerine molecule, valuable raw material for soap ____.
e: Biodiesel oil is synthesised from plant oils by removing the by-product glycerine molecule, valuable raw material for soap production. Biodiesel is a diesel-like fuel made from plant or animal fats as long-chain fatty acid esters.

q: Biodiesel oil also can be obtained from waste plant oils, e.g., oils used in ____.
e: Biodiesel oil also can be obtained from waste plant oils,, oils used in restaurants. Biodiesel is a diesel-like fuel made from plant or animal fats as long-chain fatty acid esters.

q: The combustion of fossil fuel generates sulphur compounds whereas biodiesel does ____.
e: The combustion of fossil fuel generates sulphur compounds whereas biodiesel does not. Not: biodiesel is a diesel-like fuel made from plant or animal fats as long-chain fatty acid esters.

q: Many clean water resources are becoming increasingly scarce and many of them are polluted by anthropogenic sources such as industrial purposes, agricultural waste and ____.
e: Many clean water resources are becoming increasingly scarce and many of them are polluted by anthropogenic sources such as industrial purposes, agricultural waste and household. Household is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The main purpose of wastewater treatment is to remove the various contaminants that are present in the ____.
e: The main purpose of wastewater treatment is to remove the various contaminants that are present in the wastewater. Wastewater is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The green materials such as agricultural waste adsorbent, activated carbon, and rice husk-derived ceramic materials are usually applied in the wastewater treatment ____.
e: The green materials such as agricultural waste adsorbent, activated carbon, and rice husk-derived ceramic materials are usually applied in the wastewater treatment system. System is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The photocatalysts binary metal oxides nanomaterials are also used to mineralise, decompose, and oxidise the pollutants from ____.
e: The photocatalysts binary metal oxides nanomaterials are also used to mineralise, decompose, and oxidise the pollutants from wastewater. Wastewater is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Previously, tetraethyllead (TEL) was used as an anti-knocking ____.
e: Previously, tetraethyllead (TEL) was used as an anti-knocking agent. Agent is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Nowadays, tetraethyllead is replaced by using methyl tert-butyl ether (____).
e: Nowadays, tetraethyllead is replaced by using methyl tert-butyl ether (MTBE). Ethers have an oxygen bridged between two carbon groups and are often used as solvents.

q: Methyl tert-butyl ether is a flammable liquid that has been used as an additive for unleaded ____.
e: Methyl tert-butyl ether is a flammable liquid that has been used as an additive for unleaded petrol. Ethers have an oxygen bridged between two carbon groups and are often used as solvents.

q: Bioplastics are derived from renewable biomass sources such as corn starch, vegetable oils and ____.
e: Bioplastics are derived from renewable biomass sources such as corn starch, vegetable oils and fats. Fats is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Solvents like tetrachloroethene used in dry cleaning of clothes, pollute the groundwater and are ____.
e: Solvents like tetrachloroethene used in dry cleaning of clothes, pollute the groundwater and are carcinogenic. Carcinogenic is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In the liquid $CO_2$ cleaning process, liquid carbon dioxide and other non-toxic cleaning materials replace ____.
e: In the liquid CO2 cleaning process, liquid carbon dioxide and other non-toxic cleaning materials replace tetrachloroethene. Tetrachloroethene is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Dry cleaners pressurise and then liquefy $CO_2$ gas to make it a powerful solvent for cleaning clothing ____.
e: Dry cleaners pressurise and then liquefy CO2 gas to make it a powerful solvent for cleaning clothing items. Items is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Green chemistry can design chemical products and processes that reduce or eliminate the use or generation of hazardous ____.
e: Green chemistry can design chemical products and processes that reduce or eliminate the use or generation of hazardous substances. Green chemistry designs products and processes so they make less hazardous waste.

q: Large amounts of adipic acid are used each year for the production of nylon, polyurethanes, lubricants and ____.
e: Large amounts of adipic acid are used each year for the production of nylon, polyurethanes, lubricants and plasticisers. Plasticisers is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Benzene, a compound with convinced carcinogenic properties, is a standard substrate for the production of adipic ____.
e: Benzene, a compound with convinced carcinogenic properties, is a standard substrate for the production of adipic acid. Acid is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Glucose can be converted into adipic acid by an enzyme discovered in genetically modified ____.
e: Glucose can be converted into adipic acid by an enzyme discovered in genetically modified bacteria. Enzymes are protein catalysts that speed specific biochemical reactions.

q: Hexavalent chromium plating produces several by-products which are considered as hazardous waste, including lead chromates and barium ____.
e: Hexavalent chromium plating produces several by-products which are considered as hazardous waste, including lead chromates and barium sulphate. Sulphate is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Hexavalent chromium itself is a hazardous substance and ____.
e: Hexavalent chromium itself is a hazardous substance and carcinogen. Carcinogen is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Trivalent chromium is another method of decorative chrome plating, and is considered as an environmentally friendly alternative to hexavalent ____.
e: Trivalent chromium is another method of decorative chrome plating, and is considered as an environmentally friendly alternative to hexavalent chromium. Chromium is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Trivalent chromium plating uses chromium sulphate or chromium chloride as its main ingredient, instead of chromium(VI) ____.
e: Trivalent chromium plating uses chromium sulphate or chromium chloride as its main ingredient, instead of chromium(VI) oxide. Oxide is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Vermilion is a dense, opaque pigment with a clear, brilliant hue originally made by grinding a powder of cinnabar (mercury(II) sulphide, ____).
e: Vermilion is a dense, opaque pigment with a clear, brilliant hue originally made by grinding a powder of cinnabar (mercury(II) sulphide, HgS). HgS is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Arsenic trisulphide ($As_2S_3$) is used as orpiment in works of art and is highly desirable as a pigment mostly in ____.
e: Arsenic trisulphide (As2S3) is used as orpiment in works of art and is highly desirable as a pigment mostly in lacquerware. Lacquerware is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Bananas are naturally high in potassium, which is a mix of isotopes, including the slightly radioactive isotope potassium-____.
e: Bananas are naturally high in potassium, which is a mix of isotopes, including the slightly radioactive isotope potassium-40. 40 is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Clove oil, mint oil, lemongrass oil, cinnamon oil, rosemary oil and oil of oregano are the best-known essential oils containing organic compounds with bioactivity against insects and other ____.
e: Clove oil, mint oil, lemongrass oil, cinnamon oil, rosemary oil and oil of oregano are the best-known essential oils containing organic compounds with bioactivity against insects and other pests. Pests is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.
